named_events.loss_description: The Syndicate has material exposure to Hurricane Ian. Hurricane Ian was the largest catastrophe loss in the syndicate in 2022 calendar year, however in 2023 uncertainty was reduced due to the claims developing in the year.

The Syndicate also has material exposure to a series of MidWest storms. If a 25% deterioration on the current selected gross ultimate loss pick was assumed the net impact would be GBP 1.0m deterioration on the 2022 year of account.

The 2021 and 2022 underwriting years of Syndicate 1856 are exposed to claims relating to the Ukraine-Russia Conflict. Through its insurance and reinsurance portfolios, the Syndicate has exposure to war on land and contingent aviation war and hull coverage for lessors. Scenarios have been modelled based on splits between contingent Hull War and War on Land, including consideration of cancellation clause impacts. The nature of any losses arising from the conflict is an uncertainty for the Syndicate's total reserves but does not increase that uncertainty significantly beyond the normal range of uncertainty for insurance liabilities at this stage of development. The booked ultimates for these losses as at 31 December 2023 are GBP 51.7 million gross of reinsurance and GBP 21.3 million net of reinsurance (inclusive of inwards and outwards RIPs).

For the 2023 underwriting year of Syndicate 1856, there is currently no net material exposure to the Israel-Gaza Conflict. This has not been reserved for separately, as it is believed this is adequately reserved for in general IBNR.

gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding for 2023 was GBP 383.6 million. The report does not explicitly state a single quantified figure for overall prior year reserve development in 2023. However, the syndicate's overall performance in 2023 was a profit of GBP 108.0 million, partly driven by "strong performance" in property reinsurance despite natural catastrophe losses. The syndicate has explicitly considered economic and excess inflation in its reserving process, uplifting outstanding claims reserves and IBNR claims. Specific events mentioned include Hurricane Ian (2022), which saw reduced uncertainty in 2023, and MidWest storms (2023), which are assumed to have caused a GBP 1.0 million deterioration on the 2022 year of account. The Ukraine-Russia Conflict continues to expose the 2021 and 2022 underwriting years, with booked ultimates of GBP 51.7 million gross and GBP 21.3 million net as of 31 December 2023, but no specific movement for 2023 was quantified. There was no net material exposure to the Israel-Gaza Conflict for the 2023 underwriting year.

We have explicitly considered economic and excess inflation in the reserving process when setting the best estimate reserves as historical data is not likely to be representative of the current environment and traditional reserving techniques do not address this.
Uplifting outstanding claims reserves by a set factor (at class of business underwriting year level).
IBNR claims have been uplifted from the Initial expected loss ratios ("IELRs") used in the reserving model.

The recent inflationary environment presents additional uncertainty, as settlement delays coupled with inflation may result in inadequate reserves being projected by actuarial techniques which do not explicitly take this environment into account.
